claim_checks.reason: ONECI institution and CNI document list jointly establish the responsible office.
CNI is a national identity title and nationality proof is explicitly listed; resident-card instructions are a distinct branch, not transferable.

PDF expressly allows either birth extract/full copy or notoriety act bearing the exact mention « en vue de l’établissement de la CNI »; less-than-two-years heading applies to the birth justification. Not a passport rule.

Less-than-two-year nationality certificate and receipts are listed. Page says receipt of enrolment; PDF says payment receipt for all request types. These are stage-specific, not proof that enrolment precedes itself.
PDF explicitly limits profession proof to specified professions and marriage evidence to married women; no universal extra document inferred.
The source disagreement in wording is real: page « Si possible », PDF « recommandé », FAQ parental CNI without that qualifier. FAQ omission of qualifier does not prove a universal obligation.
Page and FAQ request nationality in renewal; PDF renewal list omits it. This is an omission, not an explicit prohibition or proof that nationality is unnecessary.
The sources document the staged pathway, payment receipt and collection ID/message; no live enrolment or transaction was tested.
Both portal fiches display 5000 FCFA. This supports a displayed documentary tariff only; neither fiche proves a current 2026 payable total.
First-request fiche states indeterminate and renewal fiche forty-five days; these remain non-guaranteed historical/undated indications.

Foreign birth, naturalisation and marriage branches are explicit; acquisition by declaration is discussed in FAQ. A CNI-minor branch and definitive age threshold are NOT established. FAQ minor-under-16 instructions belong to residence cards. Retain uncertainty but do not state a verified CNI-minor list.
Common portal footer says updated 08/11/2016 on both unrelated fiches; no page-specific update date located. Absence of a detected date is an audit observation, not proof no update ever occurred.
FAQ directs people to their civil-status centre, institutional page establishes ONECI coordination and portal is visibly published; copy issuance must not be confused with initial birth registration.
FAQ centre route and lost-copy letter to mairie/sous-préfecture support locating the existing act and specifying a copy; cannot replace registration or supplementary judgment.
Lost/destroyed-copy fiche explicitly requests a letter with applicant/parents names, birth date and reason. Scope is that particular recovery route.
Portal explicitly has NNI, extract-number and other branches plus document uploads. HTML presence alone cannot establish which hidden uploads are required for each chosen branch.
Centre route and online search/tracking after payment are described. Form mainly speaks of certificate downloading; do not promise downloadable birth extract equivalence or tested issuance.
Lost-copy fiche displays Néant and Non déterminé only for that route. It does not establish ordinary copies are universally free, nor current fees.
FAQ says online birth requests unavailable while public portal and request page exist. This is a documented availability discrepancy, not proof that the full service works.
Two distinct request types appear in the select list; no equivalence or receiving-administration acceptance statement was found.

Homepage assigns birth-location jurisdiction for Ivorians born locally/foreigners with birth registered locally and DACP for stated foreign-born/resident profiles. Ministry page confirms platform provenance, not the routing details itself.
Bulletin n°3 is explicitly strictly personal on homepage; form contains centre/identity and jurisdiction summary. The profile must be correct; this page is not a ruleset for bulletins 1 or 2.
Form expressly asks to upload original birth act plus centre, act number and civil references; uploading a scan is not surrender of the physical original.
Both sources condition marriage act on absent marriage mention. Other form branches include separation or unknown-parent evidence; do not mark every hidden upload universally mandatory.
Form contains « Avez-vous une CNI ? Oui Non »; this supports a non-universal CNI inference only for the consulted route, not acceptance of all identity-free requests.

Static form contains staged entries, confirmation and payment summary; homepage describes digital-only issue and follow-up. A 2025-election warning in static modal is not an established general eligibility condition.

Homepage lists 2500 rights for the three specified 2500 profiles plus 500 service. Main-profile form independently displays 2500+500=3000 (arithmetic checked). Form alone does not prove other profiles. Payment-provider extras unconfirmed.

Homepage specifically displays 10000 rights for foreigner born abroad residing in Côte d’Ivoire, plus general 500 service line. Record deliberately describes rights, NOT a 10000 all-inclusive total and not the main profile.
Casier-central fiche displays 24 h; ministry report of 20 April 2026 states 80% of delivered acts under 72 h. Population/time basis differs; neither guarantees an individual digital-casier deadline.
Profile/jurisdiction must match homepage and form, and payment summary does not establish extra payment costs or a current guaranteed delay. No page-own update date found; no transaction performed.

Government fiche explicitly says police-controlled issue by SNEDAI, exclusively responsible for edition; official PDF is headed DST/Sous-direction PAF. SNEDAI is an operator, not the police authority.

Government fiche establishes Ivorian citizenship; operator explicitly labels first-request national-by-origin adults «18 ans et Plus», with valid CNI. This is operational profile scope, not a general civil-majority ruling.

Adult-with-CNI first-request list explicitly includes recent photo, valid CNI copy/original, original birth extract and receipt or emailed documents. Platform FAQ confirms printing appointment/receipt/form for online route.
Operational first-request adult section expressly asks traders for registry and drivers for work attestation; marriage act is for wives wishing to use spouse surname.

FAQ discusses nationality certificate and parent ID; form has matching generic checkboxes. Adult-with-valid-CNI operator list does not enumerate them. Omission is not an explicit waiver: preserve requirement uncertainty without treating every checkbox as cumulative.

Government fiche specifies personal control/biometrics, enrolment receipt and collection; platform describes online account/form/payment/appointment and printing. Merely reporting pathway; no action performed.
Both government fiche and operational page display 40000 FCFA domestic rights. No date-specific current-tariff confirmation or all-inclusive total; no diaspora extrapolation.
All sources tie 72 hours to police validation, not start of request/payment/appointment. This supports a conditional published target, never an individual guaranteed deadline.

Operator provides explicit minor, renewal, acquired-nationality and missing-CNI branches. Domestic-versus-embassy navigation exists, but cited pages do not establish a complete diaspora list. FAQ does not independently prove each named branch. Preserve as scope warning, not a verified exhaustive list.

Bank lists diverge: government/FAQ BACI+Ecobank versus operational prose also NSIA; collection FAQ says personal-only while platform allows police-approved proxy. Some platform wording is about use not collection: do not manufacture another conflict from that ambiguous sentence.
Portal body explicitly says diplomatic or service passport; this is valid exclusion evidence for the ordinary-passport workflow.

Category-B fiche identifies CGI service; article names DGTTC and operator participants; publication links ministry-hosted CGI/Quipux brochure. Hosting/operator attribution is not independent tariff-making authority.
B fiche expressly states 18 and over with successful code/driving examinations and lists medical fitness certificate. Do not generalize age to other categories.
Brochure initial-registration section explicitly lists original identity used at driving-school enrolment and original school-registration attestation.
New-permit issue section lists readable identity, theory/practice certificates and registration-attestation copies, originals presented.
B fiche expressly requires medical certificate; brochure new-issue list omits it. Omission is not evidence it is unnecessary. Exact stage/validity not established and remain to confirm.

Registration and post-exam issue are explicit, while school training is inferred from driving-school registration and successful exams rather than a complete staged procedure in these sources. Administrative edition is not the whole driving-school journey.

B fiche shows 23500; brochure category-B row aligns ENREG.16000 / EDITION7500; arithmetic checked:16000+7500=23500. These are documentary administrative components, not a 2026 all-inclusive driving-school price; never add them again to 23500.
B fiche says 01 mois minimum under delivery deadline. Published indication only, not verified full journey or guaranteed 2026 time.
Neither B fiche nor brochure proves total tuition, retake/medical fees or full elapsed time. Retain non-confirmation; do not infer zero omitted costs.

Actual fetched PDF metadata ModDate D:20210729112258Z confirms July 2021 technical modification. Creation date May 2021 also present. Neither is proof of publication date, currency of tariffs or 2026 applicability.
Format-conversion fiche explicitly targets existing permit holders, distinguishes paper/digital tariffs and one-day target; not first candidature or category-B issue.
